extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: A large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based mocap datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using the SMPL body model.
extraction.license: Creative Commons Attribution 2.1 Japan License (for Eyes Japan data); other datasets have specific licenses or were obtained privately/publicly as noted in acknowledgments.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black
extraction.publisher: Meshcapade GmbH, MPI for Intelligent Systems, York University, MPI for Informatics
extraction.citeAs: Mahmood, N., Ghorbani, N., Troje, N.F., Pons-Moll, G., & Black, M.J. (2019). AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was created by unifying 15 existing motion capture datasets. Some were downloaded from the internet, others were obtained privately, and some (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab, SSM) were recorded by the authors. The SSM dataset was recorded using an OptiTrack mocap system synchronized with a 4D scanning system.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: The paper notes inherent problems with mocap such as swapped and mislabeled markers, which were manually inspected and corrected or held out. It also discusses handling missing markers by adjusting pose prior weights based on the number of visible markers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: 15 different optical marker-based motion capture datasets containing sparse markers (ranging from 37 to 91 markers per dataset). Additionally, a novel dataset (SSM) consisting of dense 3D meshes in motion captured with a 4D scanner and traditional marker-based mocap.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Not explicitly stated for the original 15 datasets. The SSM dataset collection timeframe is not explicitly stated, but the paper was published in April 2019.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The MoSh++ method was used to convert mocap data into realistic 3D human meshes represented by the SMPL body model. This involved fitting the SMPL/DMPL body model to observed mocap markers to recover body shape, pose, and soft-tissue dynamics. The process included two stages of optimization: Stage I for shape and latent marker positions, and Stage II for pose and soft-tissue coefficients per frame.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Manual inspection of results to correct or hold out problems due to swapped and mislabeled markers. Hyperparameters for the MoSh++ fitting process were tuned using cross-validation on the SSM dataset. The data was unified into a common format including SMPL 3D shape parameters (16 dimensions), DMPL soft tissue coefficients (8 dimensions), and full SMPL pose parameters (90 dimensions).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset does not involve human annotation of labels in the traditional sense. Instead, it involves automated fitting of a body model to marker data. The 'ground truth' for evaluating the fitting method (MoSh++) was provided by synchronized 4D body scans in the SSM dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The accuracy of the reconstruction was evaluated by measuring the scan-to-model distance between the estimated 3D body meshes and the ground truth 3D scans from the SSM dataset.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++ (an extension of MoSh), SMPL body model, DMPL model, MANO hand model, Chumpy (autodifferentiation package), TensorFlow (mentioned for potential future runtime improvements).
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available at http://amass.is.tue.mpg.de. The authors state they will support the community in adding new captures and will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by the community.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset contains 3D body shapes and poses of 346 subjects. While not explicitly listing attributes like age or gender, 3D body scans and poses can be considered sensitive biometric data. Two subjects in the SSM dataset were professional models who signed modeling contracts.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to enable machine learning for applications in animation and computer vision, addressing the limitation of existing small and limited mocap datasets. It aims to provide a rich, unified resource for training deep learning models.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset unifies 15 existing datasets which may have their own biases regarding the types of motions, subjects, and marker sets used. The paper notes that previous attempts to merge datasets often normalized body proportions, which this dataset avoids to retain richness, but this may still reflect biases in the source datasets.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time. The dataset relies on optical marker-based mocap, which can suffer from marker occlusion and soft-tissue artifacts (though MoSh++ attempts to recover these). The hand articulation accuracy could not be quantitatively evaluated due to lack of ground-truth data. The dataset does not include facial mocap markers.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. Specifically for animation, visualization, and generating training data for deep learning models in computer vision.
